prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Business Rules Registry: thresholds, connection/gate/towing/stand/swap rules, border states, CTT tolerance, infrastructure events, connection-risk tie-breaker permission per state. Modes: Normal; Adverse Weather; Capacity Reduction(binding metering; RFM may suspend swaps); Recovery; Slot Compliance; Winter(MBO confirms); Contingency Fallback(ADM declares after RFM, Tower Supervisor, SSE; entry: auth/time-sync loss, corrupted or mismatched data, Alert Distribution Hub tolerance; exit: stable service, consistent data, access, leads agree; ADM closes in Foxglove). Fallback: Foxglove down→Digital Briefing Room; Marlinstone/CAM unreliable→RFM uses last verified Airport Capacity Plan; Blueharbor down→Slot Coordinator manual sheet at Contingency Operations Console, keeps last valid CTT unless safety/capacity/curfew/regulatory; revised CTT needs Tower Supervisor and Ramp Control Lead; AOC, Aircraft Operator Rep readback; Ironleaf, Ramp Movement Board advisory; Emberline monitor-only. Before automation returns, Slot Coordinator reconciles manual record with Slot Allocation Engine, conflicts in Collaborative Decision Log; Performance Analytics Warehouse receives outage timeline, manual record, milestones for Post Operations Report. Connection risk: secondary advisory signal, never replaces capacity/safety, no CTT entitlement. AOC sends Passenger Misconnect Count; Airline Interface Adapter validates timeliness, flight, ownership; Data Governance Steward sets aggregation (no names/bookings/itineraries); Marlinstone combines with readiness, banks, arrival variability for departure sensitivity; Slot Allocation Engine keeps policy, runway, airspace, Ground Delay Program as controlling; tie-breaker only if Registry permits; Departure Metering Service recommends hold/release/resequence only within runway/surface envelope; Tower Supervisor may reject; Ramp Control Lead checks Ramp Movement Board; ADM views Airport CDM Portal. Actors: RFM=Regional Flow Manager; Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison; Tower Supervisor; ADM=Airport Duty Manager; Ramp Control Lead; Ground Handling Dispatcher; Aircraft Operator Rep; AOC=Airline Operations Coordinator(TOBT); Slot Coordinator; NOL=Network Operations Liaison; SSE=System Support Engineer; Emergency Response Coordinator; Deicing Coordinator; MBO=Meteorology Briefing Officer; Data Governance Steward. Parts: Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform;

New part:
S752: The system records these actions as operational context rather than as passenger service tasks assigned to the airport flow management process.
S753: The Regional Flow Manager may consider a recovery action credible only when it is aligned with a valid Target Off Block Time, crew availability status, and confirmed aircraft readiness.
S754: If an airline indicates a recovery plan that depends on unrealistic turnaround timing, the Demand Prediction Service discounts the associated connection benefit.
S755: During Adverse Weather Mode, passenger disruption indicators are normally given less influence because the Capacity Assessment Module and Sector Load Monitor have reduced flexibility to absorb discretionary changes.
S756: During Recovery Phase, the same indicators can have greater practical value because metering margins may exist after the primary capacity constraint has begun to clear.
S757: The Arrival Regulation Console may show inbound connection pressure as context for arrival rate discussions, but it does not convert passenger handling needs into a separate arrival priority scheme.
S758: The Common Situation Display presents passenger disruption cues with clear labeling so that participants understand they are decision-support indicators, not commands.
S759: Every accepted use of connection-risk information in a metering decision is recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the responsible actor, rationale, and affected flight interval.
S760: The Performance Analytics Warehouse compares later delay outcomes with the logged rationale to determine whether the advisory use of passenger disruption data improved recovery performance.
S761: This approach keeps the primary system function focused on safe, efficient, and transparent traffic flow management while still allowing airline recovery information to inform proportionate metering choices.
S762: Cybersecurity for the Regional Flow Platform is based on centrally managed identities, explicit authorization, and traceable operational actions.
S763: The Identity Access Service is the authoritative source for user accounts, service accounts, role memberships, authentication policies, and session lifecycle controls.
S764: Each named operational user shall authenticate with an individually assigned identity before accessing the Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room, or any operational console.
S765: Shared operational accounts are not permitted for routine use because they prevent reliable attribution during time-critical flow management decisions.
S766: The Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, and Airline Operations Coordinator receive role profiles that reflect their normal operational responsibilities.
S767: Role profiles shall grant the minimum access needed to view, propose, approve, or administer operational data within the Regional Flow Platform.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
